derivation: D.3 assigns each comparison one EVAL-PROT branch and one PCOMP bundle
the bundle table expands to the exact applicable PCOMP set
D.2 maps each PCOMP to its required raw closure and its inapplicability condition
the union over the PCOMP set is the required-item vector for that comparison
parser_notes: D.2 is read by section boundary. Filtering its rows on the literal ART- in the closure column lost the 14 PCOMPs that name their fields directly; the protocol's E-COMP-001 audit states all 23 carry a D.2 row, which is what the section contains.

D.3 spans two tables. The registry that assigns branches ends where D.3.1's seven-axis audit begins, and that audit repeats every CMP id with a MATCH column, so reading to the section end silently replaced every branch with the string MATCH.
